subject: Conditional recovery obligations and RPO tier carveout request
messages:
From: Morgan Patel <morgan.patel@clearwaterfin.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@clearwaterfin.com
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA request: multi-region recovery obligations (RPO carveout)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Clearwater is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we move to procurement, our compliance group flagged a gap in the multi-region recovery commitments. We operate a primary region in us-west and a cold-replica region in us-east with asynchronous replication for a subset of batch workloads. That means during a full-region failover we can tolerate an RTO of up to 6 hours but our effective RPO for the cold-replica workloads is larger (~4 hours) because of the replication window.

Clearwater's security and risk team is asking whether Redwood can accept a conditional RPO carveout for those workloads (listed in the attachment) and include explicit audit/logging commitments during the failover window. They also want clarity on the compensation/credits if we miss the agreed RTO bound during a declared multi-region switchover.

I attached a brief that enumerates the affected services (PCI scope) and our preferred language. Can you point me to how Redwood typically handles these conditional recovery obligations and whether a contract amendment is possible?

Thanks,
Morgan
Morgan Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager, Clearwater Financial
Morgan.Patel@clearwaterfin.com
Attachment: PCI-Clearwater-SLA-Request.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Patel <morgan.patel@clearwaterfin.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2025 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request: multi-region recovery obligations (RPO carveout)

Hi Morgan — appreciate the clear writeup and the attachment. Short answers: yes, we can consider a conditional carveout for cold-replica workloads, but we need to lock in three things up front: the explicit list of endpoints/services in scope, acceptable RTO/RPO bands for each tier, and a compensating observability commitment (audit events + failover trace retention).

I'm looping in Kimberly (contracts) and Karthik (product infra) to scope the draft amendment and evaluate operational feasibility. Kimberly — can your team draft a narrow amendment that limits the carveout to the services enumerated in Morgan's PDF and defines the credit formula for a missed RTO? Karthik — can you confirm whether the existing asynchronous replication scheme will allow a 6-hour RTO and what mitigation steps (prefetching, expanded KV caching) we might apply during switchover?

Morgan — we'll aim to return a first-pass amendment and runbook within 2 business days. If you have hard constraints for logging retention or audit proof (e.g., 90 days of tamper-evident logs) call that out now so we can bake it in.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Morgan Patel <morgan.patel@clearwaterfin.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Mar 2025 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request: multi-region recovery obligations (RPO carveout)

Hi all,

Attached is a proposed SLA amendment (draft) that narrowly scopes a conditional RPO carveout for the named cold-replica workloads. Key bullets: 
- Carveout applies only to the services listed in the customer's attachment (Annex A).
- Declared multi-region switchover = event where primary region is unavailable for > 30 minutes and product confirms failover initiation.
- Agreed RTO for carved-out workloads: 6 hours; agreed RPO: up to 4 hours for async-replicated workloads.
- Observability: Redwood will provide a failover incident package including a timeline, debug logs, and a tamper-evident audit bundle retained for 90 days.
- Credits: if Redwood misses the RTO bound for carved-out workloads, credits are prorated based on affected tokens/minutes (formula in section 3).

Karthik — product/infra comment needed on two items before we mark this as internal-ready: 1) whether we can commit to the 90-day tamper-evident retention for the audit bundle (S3+WORM style) and 2) whether the credit formula is operationally testable.

Morgan — please review and flag any redlines. If legal wants to run edits, include the minimal tracked-change doc and we'll keep the amendment tightly scoped.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-sla-amendment-draft.docx

Thanks — the draft is a helpful start. A few notes from our side after an internal review: 
- Clearwater can accept the 6-hour RTO and 4-hour RPO for the specified cold-replica workloads provided Redwood confirms the 90-day tamper-evident audit bundle and a post-incident forensic packet within 48 hours of event close.
- For credits, our finance team would prefer a guaranteed minimum credit floor for high-severity events (we can discuss a $Xk floor in negotiation), but we won't block moving forward on a narrow amendment.
- We've attached a small evidence/fields spreadsheet that our audit team will use to verify the incident package contents.

If you can confirm Karthik's operational sign-off on the 90-day retention and the timing for the forensic packet, we can route this through Clearwater legal and procurement next week.

Best,
Morgan
